files.body:
# Workflow 2.1.3.1 · Specify & Classify Requirements

Derive requirements from each need, classify them into four classes, give every NFR a number, separate constraints and quality-check the set.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-3-1-specify.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-3-1-run-specify`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-3-1-specify
title: "Specify & Classify Requirements"
owner: "Business analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/needs-register.md"
  - "docs/constraint-log.md"
  - "docs/feasibility-assessment.md"
preconditions:
  - "Needs validated"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Derive candidates from each need"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-3-1-s1-derive-candidates-from-each-need
    skills: [use-cases, requirements-workshop]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Classify into the four classes"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-3-1-s2-classify-into-the-four-classes
    skills: [requirement-classification]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Quantify NFRs per quality attribute"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-3-1-s3-quantify-nfrs-per-quality-attribute
    skills: [quality-attribute-scenarios, planguage]
    reviewers: [performance-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, ai-reviewer, security-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, operations-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/qa-drivers.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "No number yet → TBD with owner and date": s4
  - id: s4
    do: "Separate constraints & merge duplicates"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-3-1-s4-separate-constraints-and-merge-duplicates
    skills: [requirement-classification]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/constraint-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Conflicts with a constraint → architect": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Passes the 29148 quality check?"
    owner: "Independent reviewer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Independent reviewer decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Ambiguous or compound → rewrite": s2
      "Infeasible requirement → sponsor": stop
gate: "Requirements review"
criteria:
  - "Singular, verifiable, feasible"
  - "Every NFR quantified"
checks:
  - "Peer review"
  - "Testability check"
on_failure:
  - "Give each a number and a condition or delete it"
  - "Ask whether a test could pass or fail on it — if not, it's a constraint"
rework: "Fails the quality check → rewrite"
outputs:
  - "docs/requirements-spec.md"
  - "docs/qa-drivers.md"
handoff: "Requirements specification & quality-attribute drivers → 2.1.4 Trace, Validate & Baseline"
learning:
  - "NFRs found later that were missed here"
```

files.title: Workflow 2.1.4.1 · Trace & Baseline Requirements
files.body:
# Workflow 2.1.4.1 · Trace & Baseline Requirements

Trace every now-horizon requirement both ways, validate it with stakeholders in scenarios and approve a versioned baseline under change control.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-4-1-baseline.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-4-1-run-baseline`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-4-1-baseline
title: "Trace & Baseline Requirements"
owner: "Business analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-spec.md"
  - "docs/needs-register.md"
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
preconditions:
  - "Requirements review passed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Build the traceability matrix"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s1-build-the-traceability-matrix
    skills: [requirements-traceability, traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Walk stakeholders through scenarios"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s2-walk-stakeholders-through-scenarios
    skills: [scenario-walkthrough]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/review-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Outcomes unattainable → DISCOVER": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Mark horizons & log open questions"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s3-mark-horizons-and-log-open-questions
    skills: [rolling-wave-planning]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/open-questions.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Complete enough for the now horizon?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Gap or orphan → fix the trace": s1
      "Unowned TBD → sponsor": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Approve & version the baseline"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s4-approve-and-version-the-baseline
    skills: [requirements-baselining, requirements-change-control]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Requirements baseline"
criteria:
  - "Bidirectional trace for the now horizon"
  - "Every TBD owned and dated"
checks:
  - "Trace check"
  - "Scenario walkthrough"
on_failure:
  - "Move later-horizon items back to 'coarse'"
  - "Delete orphans or find their need — explicitly"
rework: "Gap or orphan → fix the trace and re-validate"
outputs:
  - "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/open-questions.md"
handoff: "Requirements baseline, traceability matrix & open questions log → 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation (and Handle a Requirement Change from now on)"
learning:
  - "Requirements changed within a month of baseline"
```

files.title: Workflow 2.1.4.2 · Handle a Requirement Change
files.body:
# Workflow 2.1.4.2 · Handle a Requirement Change

Once a baseline exists, every change is logged, its impact on scope, forecast and cost analysed, decided by the right person and traced.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-4-2-change-control.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-4-2-run-change-control`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-4-2-change-control
title: "Handle a Requirement Change"
owner: "Business analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
preconditions:
  - "Baseline v1.0 approved"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Log the change request"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s1-log-the-change-request
    skills: [requirements-change-control]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-request.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse impact on scope, forecast & cost"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s2-analyse-impact-on-scope-forecast-and-cost
    skills: [requirements-traceability, traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, quality-reviewer, synthesiser, challenger]
    output: "docs/change-request.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Accept, defer or reject?"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Impact unclear → analyse again": s2
      "Deferred → logged for the next horizon, owners told": s4
      "Changes outcome, cost or date beyond tolerance → sponsor": authority
      "Rejected → reason recorded": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Update baseline & trace"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s3-update-baseline-and-trace
    skills: [requirements-baselining]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Notify affected owners"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s4-notify-affected-owners
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Change decided"
criteria:
  - "Every change has a request, an impact and a decision"
checks:
  - "Version diff against the last baseline"
on_failure:
  - "Restore the last version and raise the request properly"
  - "Re-run the forecast with the change"
rework: "Impact unclear → analyse again with engineering"
outputs:
  - "docs/change-request.md"
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
handoff: "Updated baseline & trace → 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation and any downstream owner (DESIGN, BUILD)"
learning:
  - "Change rate per month and its sources — learning log"
```

# Workflow 2.3.3.1 · Run the Delivery Forecast

Simulate delivery from sizes and throughput, read dates at 50% and 85% confidence and publish them with their assumptions.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-3-3-1-forecast.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-3-3-1-run-forecast`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-3-3-1-forecast
title: "Run the Delivery Forecast"
owner: "Delivery lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/estimate-sheet.md"
  - "docs/capacity-plan.md"
  - "docs/dependency-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Sizes agreed"
  - "Capacity confirmed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Total remaining work per release"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-3-1-s1-total-remaining-work-per-release
    skills: [reference-class-forecasting]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Simulate throughput (Monte Carlo)"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-3-1-s2-simulate-throughput-monte-carlo
    skills: [monte-carlo-forecasting, probabilistic-forecasting]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Read 50% / 85% dates & assumptions"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-3-1-s3-read-50-85-dates-and-assumptions
    skills: [cone-of-uncertainty, sensitivity-analysis]
    reviewers: [vendor-reviewer, finance-reviewer, synthesiser, challenger]
    output: "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Single date demanded → sponsor": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Inputs and assumptions sound?"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Engineering lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Inputs wrong → fix and re-run": s1
      "No useful window → business case": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish forecast with ranges"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-3-1-s4-publish-forecast-with-ranges
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Forecast reviewed"
criteria:
  - "50% and 85% dates"
  - "Assumptions listed"
checks:
  - "Team input review"
  - "Back-test"
on_failure:
  - "Restore the honest inputs and show the gap"
  - "Add the historic split allowance and re-run"
rework: "Inputs wrong → fix and re-run"
outputs:
  - "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
handoff: "Delivery forecast → 2.3.4 Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity"
learning:
  - "Forecast vs actual delivery date"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 2.3.4.1 · Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity

Lay out the ways to make scope, date and capacity fit, cost each, let the sponsor choose and record what gave.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-3-4-1-reconcile.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-3-4-1-run-reconcile`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-3-4-1-reconcile
title: "Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity"
owner: "Delivery lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
  - "docs/scope-statement.md"
  - "docs/cost-estimate.md"
preconditions:
  - "Forecast reviewed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Compare forecast with targets"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-4-1-s1-compare-forecast-with-targets
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Generate & cost options"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-4-1-s2-generate-and-cost-options
    skills: [trade-off-analysis, moscow, sensitivity-analysis, fixed-time-flexible-scope]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer, vendor-reviewer, finance-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/tradeoff-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Sponsor chooses an option that fits?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "No option acceptable → new options": s2
      "Above sponsor's limit → portfolio board": authority
      "Nothing fits → business case rework or no-go": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Record the trade-off"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-3-4-1-s3-record-the-trade-off
    reviewers: [business-reviewer]
    output: "docs/tradeoff-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4

    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Plan fits"
criteria:
  - "Three options costed"
  - "Fit at 85%"
checks:
  - "Finance check"
on_failure:
  - "Restore quality and re-cost"
  - "Write the decision record the same day"
rework: "No acceptable option → generate new options"
outputs:
  - "docs/tradeoff-record.md"
  - "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
handoff: "Scope–time–capacity trade-off & re-forecast → 2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning"
learning:
  - "Trade-offs that had to be revisited"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 2.4.3.1 · Plan Releases & Site Rollout

Group slices into releases, set windows clear of freezes, plan a site-by-site rollout behind flags with progression criteria and agree it with operations.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-4-3-1-releases.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-4-3-1-run-releases`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-4-3-1-releases
title: "Plan Releases & Site Rollout"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-roadmap.md"
  - "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
  - "docs/dependency-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Now horizon agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Group slices into releases"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-4-3-1-s1-group-slices-into-releases
    skills: [release-planning]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Set windows around freezes"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-4-3-1-s2-set-windows-around-freezes
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, infrastructure-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Window clashes with a freeze → change authority": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Plan rollout by site with criteria"
    owner: "Delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-4-3-1-s3-plan-rollout-by-site-with-criteria
    skills: [progressive-delivery, canary-release, feature-toggles]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, domain-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1

  - "Releases that slipped their window"
```

# Workflow 2.5.1.1 · Build the Business Case

Appraise the options, model benefits and costs as ranges, compute NPV and payback with sensitivities, and write the case finance will sign.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-5-1-1-business-case
title: "Build the Business Case"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/sizing-model.md"
  - "docs/cost-estimate.md"
  - "docs/delivery-forecast.md"
  - "docs/release-plan.md"
preconditions:
  - "Plan reconciled"
  - "Release plan agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Appraise options incl. do nothing"
    owner: "Product manager"

    skills: [options-appraisal]
    reviewers: [business-reviewer, vendor-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/options-appraisal.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Model benefits with ramp-up"
    owner: "Finance partner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-5-1-1-s2-model-benefits-with-ramp-up
    skills: [benefits-realisation-management]
    reviewers: [finance-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/benefits-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Model costs; compute NPV & payback"
    owner: "Finance partner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-5-1-1-s3-model-costs-compute-npv-and-payback
    skills: [net-present-value, cost-of-delay]
    reviewers: [finance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/benefits-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Run sensitivities"
    owner: "Finance partner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-5-1-1-s4-run-sensitivities
    skills: [sensitivity-analysis]
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/benefits-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end

    decision: "Finance validates the model?"

    checkpoint: review-at-end

  - "Ranges with sources"
  - "Three options including do nothing"
checks:
  - "Finance review"
  - "Sensitivity"
on_failure:
  - "Show low / likely / high and lead with likely"
  - "Add three years of licences and support"
rework: "Assumption disputed → re-model"
outputs:
  - "docs/business-case.md"
  - "docs/benefits-model.md"
  - "docs/options-appraisal.md"
handoff: "Business case, benefits model & options appraisal → 2.5.2 Secure Funding & Resourcing"
learning:
  - "Benefit assumptions later disproven (EVOLVE)"
```

# Workflow 2.5.4.1 · Hold the Commitment Decision

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act II PLAN · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
PLAN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## PLAN: Turn a validated opportunity into a scoped, prioritised, estimated, sequenced and funded commitment that DESIGN can start on.
- **2.1 Requirements Engineering** — gate: Requirements Baseline. Produces: Outcome & success-criteria map, Business requirements specification, Stakeholder needs register, Requirements specification, Traceability matrix, Requirements baseline.
- **2.2 Scope & Prioritisation** — gate: Scope Agreement. Produces: Scope statement, Story map, Initiative breakdown, Slice plan, WSJF scoring sheet, Product backlog.
- **2.3 Estimation & Capacity** — gate: Forecast Agreed. Produces: Estimate sheet, Capacity plan, Delivery forecast, Scope–time–capacity trade-off.
- **2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning** — gate: Roadmap Agreed. Produces: Dependency register, Release roadmap, Release plan, Roadmap briefing.
- **2.5 Investment & Approval** — gate: Commitment. Produces: Business case, Funding confirmation, Commitment conditions, Commitment decision record, Committed initiative pack, Learning log, PLAN retrospective.
- Act gate: **Commitment** — decided by: Sponsor commits within their limit; portfolio board above it and on escalation..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: NEED → RQ → EPC → FEA → EST → RMP → BC → CMT → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `plan-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.
Access: Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
team.GUARDRAILS.md:
# Guardrails & hooks — Plan

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Product team
- Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
- Watch for: Each person's agent producing inconsistent artifacts — use the shared templates
- Watch for: Discovery and delivery drifting apart

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### PLAN
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Quality is never the variable that gives
- Investment thresholds and delegated authority
- Incremental funding against evidence
- Funding envelope and delegated authority
- Team capacity
- Vendor connector by June
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.1 Requirements Engineering
- No requirement without a source need
- Constraints kept separate from requirements
- Change after baseline only through change control
- Requirements stored and versioned in the requirements tool
- ERP import API only
- Baseline only the next horizon

### 2.1.1 Derive Business Requirements & Outcomes
- No solution words in outcomes
- Measurement is a requirement, not an afterthought
- Every benefit has a named business owner
- Baseline data availability

### 2.1.2 Elicit Stakeholder & User Needs
- Needs are stated in solution-free language
- The negative question is asked of every group
- Personal data in notes handled per privacy policy
- Stakeholder availability

### 2.1.3 Specify Functional & Non-Functional Requirements
- One behaviour per requirement
- No requirement without a source need
- NFRs reviewed by engineering, security and operations
- ERP import API only
- Engineering's ability to quantify

### 2.1.4 Trace, Validate & Baseline
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Later-horizon items are not baselined
- Baseline versioned in the requirements tool
- Next horizon only

### 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation
- Requirement classes are not hierarchy levels
- Every item has a parent and an outcome
- Order reviewed at every roadmap review
- Vendor connector date
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.2.1 Define MVP & Scope Boundary
- Every in-scope item traces to a baselined requirement
- Out-of-scope list published with the scope
- Vendor connector date
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.2.2 Decompose into Epics & Features
- Requirement classes are not hierarchy levels
- Every item has a parent
- IDs follow INI → EPC → FEA
- Team boundaries

### 2.2.3 Slice for Value & Learning
- Technical work sits under a slice as tasks, never as a slice
- Slices sized to fit well inside one sprint
- Sprint length

### 2.2.4 Order by Value (WSJF)
- One ordered list — no parallel 'priority 1' lists
- Order reviewed at every roadmap review
- Relative scoring only

### 2.3 Estimation & Capacity
- No single-point dates in commitments
- Quality is never traded to fit
- Re-forecast at every sprint review
- Team size and skills
- Fixed freeze dates

### 2.3.1 Size the Work Relatively
- Estimates are not commitments
- Only the team changes a team estimate
- Uncertainty recorded with every size
- Team availability

### 2.3.2 Establish Team Capacity
- Nobody planned above 100% allocation; a focus factor applied
- Shared specialists booked through their line manager
- Headcount and budget

### 2.3.3 Forecast with Ranges
- No single-point dates in commitments
- Re-forecast at every sprint review
- Commitment dates

### 2.3.4 Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity
- Quality is not a variable — testing and the DoD are never traded away
- Trade-offs recorded in the decision log
- Fixed peak-season freeze

### 2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning
- Only the now horizon carries dates
- No rollout into a change freeze
- Monthly roadmap review
- Vendor connector by June
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.4.1 Map Dependencies & Constraints
- Critical-path dependencies reviewed weekly
- Vendor commitments go through procurement
- Vendor connector by June
- Change freeze

### 2.4.2 Build the Now / Next / Later Roadmap
- Only the now horizon carries dates
- Roadmap reviewed monthly
- Dates only on the now horizon

### 2.4.3 Plan Releases & Rollout
- No rollout into a change freeze
- Feature flag per site
- Release calendar aligned with change management
- Change freeze
- Site readiness

### 2.4.4 Publish & Align the Roadmap
- The later horizon carries no dates externally
- Roadmap reviewed monthly and after each release
- Commercially sensitive dates

### 2.5 Investment & Approval
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
- Outcomes are Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go
- Delegated authority limits
- Risk appetite statement
- Delegated authority
- Risk appetite

### 2.5.1 Build the Business Case
- Benefits counted once, with ramp-up
- Costs include three years of run
- Investment appraisal per finance policy (discount rate, horizon)
- Discount rate and horizon

### 2.5.2 Secure Funding & Resourcing
- No spend before funding is confirmed
- Vendor commitments only through procurement
- Delegated authority limits per finance policy
- Delegated authority

### 2.5.3 Confirm Risk, Compliance & Conditions
- No commitment with an unowned high risk
- Risk appetite statement
- Vendor management policy
- Risk appetite

### 2.5.4 Make the Commitment Decision
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
- Decision rights per delegated authority
- Delegated authority

team.workflows/plan-2-1-1-1-outcomes.md:
# Workflow 2.1.1.1 · Derive Outcomes & Business Requirements

Split the brief's value hypothesis into outcomes, give each a measured success criterion and write the business requirements that follow.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-1-1-outcomes.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-1-1-run-outcomes`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-1-1-outcomes
title: "Derive Outcomes & Business Requirements"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
  - "docs/decision-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Opportunity brief accepted"
  - "Sponsor available"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Read the brief & conditions aloud"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s1-read-the-brief-and-conditions-aloud
    reviewers: [business-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Brief conditions failed → back to DISCOVER": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Split the objective into outcomes"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s2-split-the-objective-into-outcomes
    skills: [goal-tree, impact-mapping, five-whys]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/outcome-map.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Pull baselines & set criteria"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s3-pull-baselines-and-set-criteria
    skills: [planguage]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer, finance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/baseline-extract.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "No data source → add a measurement requirement": s4
  - id: s4
    do: "Draft business requirements"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s4-draft-business-requirements
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/brs.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Sponsor agrees outcomes & criteria?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Disputed → re-split outcomes": s2
      "Contradicts decision record → portfolio board": authority
gate: "Outcomes agreed"
criteria:
  - "Each criterion has direction, baseline, target and source"
checks:
  - "Baseline check against source data"
on_failure:
  - "Pull a two-week baseline sample before agreeing"
  - "Rewrite each outcome as a change a named role experiences"
rework: "Sponsor disputes an outcome → re-split and re-measure"
outputs:
  - "docs/outcome-map.md"
  - "docs/brs.md"
handoff: "Outcome & success-criteria map & BRS → 2.1.2 Elicit Stakeholder & User Needs"
learning:
  - "Criteria that later proved unmeasurable"
```

# Workflow 2.1.4.1 · Trace & Baseline Requirements

Trace every now-horizon requirement both ways, validate it with stakeholders in scenarios and approve a versioned baseline under change control.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-4-1-baseline.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-4-1-run-baseline`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-4-1-baseline
title: "Trace & Baseline Requirements"
owner: "Business analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-spec.md"
  - "docs/needs-register.md"
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
preconditions:
  - "Requirements review passed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Build the traceability matrix"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s1-build-the-traceability-matrix
    skills: [requirements-traceability, traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Walk stakeholders through scenarios"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s2-walk-stakeholders-through-scenarios
    skills: [scenario-walkthrough]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/review-record.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Outcomes unattainable → DISCOVER": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Mark horizons & log open questions"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s3-mark-horizons-and-log-open-questions
    skills: [rolling-wave-planning]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/open-questions.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Complete enough for the now horizon?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Gap or orphan → fix the trace": s1
      "Unowned TBD → sponsor": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Approve & version the baseline"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-1-s4-approve-and-version-the-baseline
    skills: [requirements-baselining, requirements-change-control]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "Requirements baseline"
criteria:
  - "Bidirectional trace for the now horizon"
  - "Every TBD owned and dated"
checks:
  - "Trace check"
  - "Scenario walkthrough"
on_failure:
  - "Move later-horizon items back to 'coarse'"
  - "Delete orphans or find their need — explicitly"
rework: "Gap or orphan → fix the trace and re-validate"
outputs:
  - "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/open-questions.md"
handoff: "Requirements baseline, traceability matrix & open questions log → 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation (and Handle a Requirement Change from now on)"
learning:
  - "Requirements changed within a month of baseline"
```
team.workflows/plan-2-1-4-2-change-control.md:
# Workflow 2.1.4.2 · Handle a Requirement Change

Once a baseline exists, every change is logged, its impact on scope, forecast and cost analysed, decided by the right person and traced.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-4-2-change-control.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-4-2-run-change-control`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-4-2-change-control
title: "Handle a Requirement Change"
owner: "Business analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
preconditions:
  - "Baseline v1.0 approved"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Log the change request"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s1-log-the-change-request
    skills: [requirements-change-control]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-request.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse impact on scope, forecast & cost"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s2-analyse-impact-on-scope-forecast-and-cost
    skills: [requirements-traceability, traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, quality-reviewer, synthesiser, challenger]
    output: "docs/change-request.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Accept, defer or reject?"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Impact unclear → analyse again": s2
      "Deferred → logged for the next horizon, owners told": s4
      "Changes outcome, cost or date beyond tolerance → sponsor": authority
      "Rejected → reason recorded": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Update baseline & trace"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s3-update-baseline-and-trace
    skills: [requirements-baselining]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Notify affected owners"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-4-2-s4-notify-affected-owners
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/traceability-matrix.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "Change decided"
criteria:
  - "Every change has a request, an impact and a decision"
checks:
  - "Version diff against the last baseline"
on_failure:
  - "Restore the last version and raise the request properly"
  - "Re-run the forecast with the change"
rework: "Impact unclear → analyse again with engineering"
outputs:
  - "docs/change-request.md"
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
handoff: "Updated baseline & trace → 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation and any downstream owner (DESIGN, BUILD)"
learning:
  - "Change rate per month and its sources — learning log"
```

```yaml
    do: "Map the journey as a story map"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act II PLAN · Scale: Enterprise. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
PLAN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## PLAN: Turn a validated opportunity into a scoped, prioritised, estimated, sequenced and funded commitment that DESIGN can start on.
- **2.1 Requirements Engineering** — gate: Requirements Baseline. Produces: Outcome & success-criteria map, Business requirements specification, Stakeholder needs register, Requirements specification, Traceability matrix, Requirements baseline.
- **2.2 Scope & Prioritisation** — gate: Scope Agreement. Produces: Scope statement, Story map, Initiative breakdown, Slice plan, WSJF scoring sheet, Product backlog.
- **2.3 Estimation & Capacity** — gate: Forecast Agreed. Produces: Estimate sheet, Capacity plan, Delivery forecast, Scope–time–capacity trade-off.
- **2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning** — gate: Roadmap Agreed. Produces: Dependency register, Release roadmap, Release plan, Roadmap briefing.
- **2.5 Investment & Approval** — gate: Commitment. Produces: Business case, Funding confirmation, Commitment conditions, Commitment decision record, Committed initiative pack, Learning log, PLAN retrospective.
- Act gate: **Commitment** — decided by: Sponsor commits within their limit; portfolio board above it and on escalation..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: NEED → RQ → EPC → FEA → EST → RMP → BC → CMT → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `plan-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Enterprise
Use formal language and our approved templates. Back every claim with a reference to its evidence for audit, flag compliance, security and privacy implications, name the approver for each decision, and keep confidential details out of anything meant for wider sharing.
Access: Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.

# Guardrails & hooks — Plan

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Enterprise
- Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
- Watch for: Pasting confidential or personal data into unapproved tools
- Watch for: Agent output in audited artifacts without a human reviewer named

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### PLAN
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Quality is never the variable that gives
- Investment thresholds and delegated authority
- Incremental funding against evidence
- Funding envelope and delegated authority
- Team capacity
- Vendor connector by June
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.1 Requirements Engineering
- No requirement without a source need
- Constraints kept separate from requirements
- Change after baseline only through change control
- Requirements stored and versioned in the requirements tool
- ERP import API only
- Baseline only the next horizon

### 2.1.1 Derive Business Requirements & Outcomes
- No solution words in outcomes
- Measurement is a requirement, not an afterthought
- Every benefit has a named business owner
- Baseline data availability

### 2.1.2 Elicit Stakeholder & User Needs
- Needs are stated in solution-free language
- The negative question is asked of every group
- Personal data in notes handled per privacy policy
- Stakeholder availability

### 2.1.3 Specify Functional & Non-Functional Requirements
- One behaviour per requirement
- No requirement without a source need
- NFRs reviewed by engineering, security and operations
- ERP import API only
- Engineering's ability to quantify

### 2.1.4 Trace, Validate & Baseline
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Later-horizon items are not baselined
- Baseline versioned in the requirements tool
- Next horizon only

### 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation
- Requirement classes are not hierarchy levels
- Every item has a parent and an outcome
- Order reviewed at every roadmap review
- Vendor connector date
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.2.1 Define MVP & Scope Boundary
- Every in-scope item traces to a baselined requirement
- Out-of-scope list published with the scope

### 2.2.2 Decompose into Epics & Features
- Requirement classes are not hierarchy levels

### 2.2.3 Slice for Value & Learning
- Technical work sits under a slice as tasks, never as a slice

- One ordered list — no parallel 'priority 1' lists
- Order reviewed at every roadmap review
- Relative scoring only

### 2.3 Estimation & Capacity
- No single-point dates in commitments
- Quality is never traded to fit

- Team size and skills
- Fixed freeze dates

### 2.3.1 Size the Work Relatively
- Estimates are not commitments
- Only the team changes a team estimate
- Uncertainty recorded with every size
- Team availability

### 2.3.2 Establish Team Capacity
- Nobody planned above 100% allocation; a focus factor applied
- Shared specialists booked through their line manager
- Headcount and budget

### 2.3.3 Forecast with Ranges
- No single-point dates in commitments
- Re-forecast at every sprint review
- Commitment dates

### 2.3.4 Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity
- Quality is not a variable — testing and the DoD are never traded away

### 2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning
- Only the now horizon carries dates

### 2.4.3 Plan Releases & Rollout
- No rollout into a change freeze

- Release calendar aligned with change management
- Change freeze
- Site readiness

### 2.4.4 Publish & Align the Roadmap
- The later horizon carries no dates externally

- Commercially sensitive dates

### 2.5 Investment & Approval
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record

```yaml

title: "Derive Outcomes & Business Requirements"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
  - "docs/decision-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Opportunity brief accepted"
  - "Sponsor available"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Read the brief & conditions aloud"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s1-read-the-brief-and-conditions-aloud
    reviewers: [business-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Brief conditions failed → back to DISCOVER": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Split the objective into outcomes"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s2-split-the-objective-into-outcomes
    skills: [goal-tree, impact-mapping, five-whys]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/outcome-map.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Pull baselines & set criteria"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s3-pull-baselines-and-set-criteria
    skills: [planguage]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer, finance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/baseline-extract.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "No data source → add a measurement requirement": s4
  - id: s4
    do: "Draft business requirements"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s4-draft-business-requirements
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/brs.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Sponsor agrees outcomes & criteria?"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act II PLAN · Scale: Platform. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
PLAN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## PLAN: Turn a validated opportunity into a scoped, prioritised, estimated, sequenced and funded commitment that DESIGN can start on.
- **2.1 Requirements Engineering** — gate: Requirements Baseline. Produces: Outcome & success-criteria map, Business requirements specification, Stakeholder needs register, Requirements specification, Traceability matrix, Requirements baseline.
- **2.2 Scope & Prioritisation** — gate: Scope Agreement. Produces: Scope statement, Story map, Initiative breakdown, Slice plan, WSJF scoring sheet, Product backlog.
- **2.3 Estimation & Capacity** — gate: Forecast Agreed. Produces: Estimate sheet, Capacity plan, Delivery forecast, Scope–time–capacity trade-off.
- **2.4 Roadmap & Release Planning** — gate: Roadmap Agreed. Produces: Dependency register, Release roadmap, Release plan, Roadmap briefing.
- **2.5 Investment & Approval** — gate: Commitment. Produces: Business case, Funding confirmation, Commitment conditions, Commitment decision record, Committed initiative pack, Learning log, PLAN retrospective.
- Act gate: **Commitment** — decided by: Sponsor commits within their limit; portfolio board above it and on escalation..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: NEED → RQ → EPC → FEA → EST → RMP → BC → CMT → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `plan-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Platform
Treat other internal teams as the customers. Capture their needs as service or API contracts, and consider versioning, backward compatibility, self-service, documentation and adoption.
Access: Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.

# Guardrails & hooks — Plan

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Platform
- Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.
- Watch for: Building what the platform team finds interesting, not what consumers need
- Watch for: Breaking changes without versioning

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### PLAN
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Quality is never the variable that gives
- Investment thresholds and delegated authority
- Incremental funding against evidence
- Funding envelope and delegated authority
- Team capacity
- Vendor connector by June
- Peak-season change freeze

### 2.1 Requirements Engineering
- No requirement without a source need
- Constraints kept separate from requirements
- Change after baseline only through change control
- Requirements stored and versioned in the requirements tool
- ERP import API only
- Baseline only the next horizon

### 2.1.1 Derive Business Requirements & Outcomes

- Measurement is a requirement, not an afterthought
- Every benefit has a named business owner
- Baseline data availability

### 2.1.2 Elicit Stakeholder & User Needs

- The negative question is asked of every group
- Personal data in notes handled per privacy policy
- Stakeholder availability

### 2.1.3 Specify Functional & Non-Functional Requirements
- One behaviour per requirement
- No requirement without a source need
- NFRs reviewed by engineering, security and operations

### 2.1.4 Trace, Validate & Baseline
- Baselined requirements change only through change control
- Later-horizon items are not baselined

### 2.2 Scope & Prioritisation
- Requirement classes are not hierarchy levels

### 2.2.1 Define MVP & Scope Boundary

- Estimates are not commitments

### 2.3.2 Establish Team Capacity

- Headcount and budget

### 2.3.3 Forecast with Ranges
- No single-point dates in commitments

- Commitment dates

### 2.3.4 Reconcile Scope, Time & Capacity
- Quality is not a variable — testing and the DoD are never traded away

- Change freeze

### 2.4.4 Publish & Align the Roadmap

### 2.5 Investment & Approval
- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record

- No spend before funding is confirmed

- Risk appetite

- No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record

# Workflow 2.1.1.1 · Derive Outcomes & Business Requirements

Split the brief's value hypothesis into outcomes, give each a measured success criterion and write the business requirements that follow.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/plan-2-1-1-1-outcomes.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `plan-2-1-1-1-run-outcomes`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: plan-2-1-1-1-outcomes
title: "Derive Outcomes & Business Requirements"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
  - "docs/decision-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Opportunity brief accepted"
  - "Sponsor available"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Read the brief & conditions aloud"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s1-read-the-brief-and-conditions-aloud
    reviewers: [business-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Brief conditions failed → back to DISCOVER": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Split the objective into outcomes"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s2-split-the-objective-into-outcomes
    skills: [goal-tree, impact-mapping, five-whys]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/outcome-map.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Pull baselines & set criteria"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s3-pull-baselines-and-set-criteria
    skills: [planguage]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer, finance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/baseline-extract.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "No data source → add a measurement requirement": s4
  - id: s4
    do: "Draft business requirements"
    owner: "Business analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: plan-2-1-1-1-s4-draft-business-requirements
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/brs.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Sponsor agrees outcomes & criteria?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Disputed → re-split outcomes": s2
      "Contradicts decision record → portfolio board": authority
gate: "Outcomes agreed"
criteria:
  - "Each criterion has direction, baseline, target and source"
checks:
  - "Baseline check against source data"
on_failure:
  - "Pull a two-week baseline sample before agreeing"
  - "Rewrite each outcome as a change a named role experiences"
rework: "Sponsor disputes an outcome → re-split and re-measure"
```
